about: Every image Iron Age ships, one entry each (V59 §14). Photo entries are written by vibes-night/tools/ia-v-photos-place.mjs from the untouched originals, the build log (ia-v-photos.mjs) and the pixel measurements (ia-v-photos-check.mjs). No AI tool touched any file; every transform is listed as the command that made it. Nothing is approved: micah_approved is false on every entry.

entries.title: "Teamsters' Warning", Figs. 21-22 - Sargent, Health, Strength & Power (1904), plate at leaf 205
entries.subject: Fig. 21: the model standing with both arms flung out level; Fig. 22: the same model in a wide squat with arms folded. Halftones cut out over a flat grey panel, lettered "Teamsters' Warning".
entries.creator: Uncredited photographer; halftones made "from numerous photographs of a well-trained model" (author's preface) for D. A. Sargent, Health, Strength & Power (1904)
entries.creator_died: anonymous (no photographer named); book author Dudley Allen Sargent 1849-1924 (IA record); copyright claimant H. M. Caldwell Co. (a company)
entries.created: before publication in 1904 (the preface is dated "Cambridge, July," with the year garbled in the OCR)

first_published.venue: Dudley Allen Sargent, Health, Strength & Power (New York and Boston: H. M. Caldwell Co., 1904). Title-page verso: "Copyright, 1904, By H. M. Caldwell Co.", full-page halftone plate

entries.source_institution: Internet Archive (scan of a Brigham Young University, Harold B. Lee Library copy)
entries.rights_statement_verbatim: (none: the item record carries no rights, licenseurl or possible-copyright-status field; metadata API, retrieved 2026-09-27)
entries.pd_basis_us: Published in New York and Boston in 1904 with a copyright notice, before 1931: US term expired.
entries.pd_basis_worldwide: The photographer is not named (anonymous): the EU/UK anonymous term is 70 years from publication, 1904 + 70 = 1974. The book's author, Sargent, died 1924 (life + 70 ended 31 Dec 1994); the claimant is a company. Test 2 passes on every reading.
entries.crop_why: Fig. 21 only: the head, the arms flung out level and both hands, over the top of the grey panel. The hint's full width (x .025-.965); top at 70 px, 67 px above the hint's .03 (137 px), into the clean page margin, so the face rule clears the hair with room (the page-top view shows plain stock there); "Fig. 21." (y ~1246) and all lettering far below.

entries.clothing_check: PASS. In frame: the model's head, arms and hands, and the top of his bare chest (the plate: knitted gymnasium tights to the ankle, belt, soft shoes, bare torso; an exercise pose, not a statue pose). No nudity, no drape, no fig leaf. Unnamed model.
entries.likeness: Unnamed model; no name printed anywhere in the book that was found. No likeness constraint beyond "never imply endorsement".

face_rule.rule: a head box (hair top to chin, ear to ear, read by eye off gridded views, +-10 source px) grown 15 % of its height above and below and 10 % of its width each side must be wholly visible in every box

Any other text colour on that fallback fails (spec §5.1).

not_used.spec: design/iron-age.md §10 names it for weightLog, pending Q-Q2
not_used.why: Fails the face rule on every band box. Her head (bun top 627 to chin 897, 742-925 across, source px) grown by the rule spans 351 px; the widest band the plate allows (its crop hint, 1533 px wide, at the band's 4.98:1) is 308 px tall. Rights and clothing pass; the geometry does not. The spec's fallback, gym-naval-academy, is used (img/weight.png).

decisions_left_to_micah: Halftone pitch 6 device px (2.0 pt on the @3x thumbnail, 2.04 pt on the bands) in place of the spec's 3.0 pt (§10 pipeline step 4): at 3.0 pt an 80 pt band holds 26 dot rows and the naval plate and the thumbnail read as a checkerboard. The spec-exact set (IA_PITCH=9) is built and checked too: ~/dev/vibes-night/ia-photos/out-p9/ (all checks pass).
weightLog falls back to the naval gym (the woman plate fails the face rule), so the naval plate appears on Steps, Weight and the Vibes card, in three different crops (spec §16 names the risk).
The Sargent crop takes 67 px of plain page margin above the plate's crop hint, so the face rule clears his hair by 20 asset px rather than 7.
No scrim is baked into any file (band mode needs none; the thumbnail's is the definition's, drawn at run time).
